titolo: Zelensky's 1,300-Drone Strike: Is Russia's Crimea Lifeline Cut?
angolo: While Russia hit two Kyiv bridges, Ukraine hit Russia's most symbolic bridge: a bridge-for-bridge duel, and who says what about the damage.
descrizione: Zelensky's 1,300-Drone Strike: Is Russia's Crimea Lifeline Cut? Russia says it shot down a record 1,336 Ukrainian drones, yet the Kerch Bridge was hit and traffic halted. Hours later, Russian ballistic missiles struck two Kyiv bridges, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. We separate what is confirmed from what is only claimed, with both sides on the record. Subscribe, because this story is still moving.

scene.testo: Dawn over the Kerch Strait. A drone slams into an arch of Russia's most symbolic bridge.
Social media posts suggested about 2,000 vehicles were stuck on both sides of the crossing, though that figure is unverified.
Hours later, Kyiv's mayor said Russian ballistic missiles hit two major bridges in the capital, based on preliminary information.
Two capitals. Two sets of bridges. One question: what happens next?
Russia says it shot down 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight.
That would be the highest number of interceptions in a single aerial attack since the full-scale invasion, according to Russian figures that cannot be independently verified.
The previous record, 1,254 drones, was registered on October 29.
Russia later reported a total of 2,049 drones intercepted over 24 hours, including the 1,336 overnight figure.
Kyiv had not publicly detailed the operation, according to reports.
Russia claimed that around 600 drones were intercepted on approach to the Moscow region.
Moscow's mayor reported that 191 drones were intercepted as they approached the capital, according to the AP.
Russia's defense ministry says the drones were downed across 16 regions.
Six people were wounded in Russia's Krasnodar region, according to local authorities.
Ukraine targeted the Kerch Bridge. And that is not the whole story.

visivo.testo: Ukraine targeted the Kerch Bridge. And that is not the whole story.

scene.testo: The Kerch Bridge stretches 19 kilometers, the only direct link between Russian and Crimean transport networks.
Putin opened it in 2018, after Russia annexed Crimea in 2014.
Ukraine and most of the world call that annexation illegal.
It carries military supplies and civilians alike, across road and rail.
In October 2022, a truck bomb detonated on the bridge, killing four people and limiting its capacity for several months.
Russia responded with a massive missile barrage across Ukraine, which Putin described as retaliation.
Ukraine struck the bridge again in July 2023, with naval drones.
And again in June 2025, when the SBU said it had mined the underwater supports with over one metric ton of TNT.
After the 2023 attack, Russia installed metal barges with boom barriers and has since added further defenses, according to reports.
Yet this time, the bridge was hit anyway. Here is what each side says.

visivo.testo: Yet this time, the bridge was hit anyway. Here is what each side says.

scene.testo: Crimea's Russian-installed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed the bridge was struck and traffic restricted.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the attack caused 'insignificant damage', and bridge authorities said vehicle traffic resumed Monday evening.
Officials in Crimea said a single lane of traffic had resumed by mid-evening, roughly 17 hours after the bridge was closed, according to Reuters.
A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows signs of damage around the arch of the road crossing and possible scorch marks, TWZ reports.
TWZ also noted that state media footage of the reopening did not show the damaged arch.
One report cited by The Guardian said the arch was listing at a 15-degree angle, according to Around Prague.
That is one report. The extent of the damage remains unclear.

visivo.testo: THE EXTENT OF DAMAGE REMAINS UNCLEAR

scene.testo: Then came a second attack on the bridge, in less than 24 hours, Aksyonov said on Telegram.
Sevastopol's Russian-installed governor urged residents not to travel to mainland Russia via the bridge.
Now, a look at the Ukrainian president Moscow blames for the strikes.
Volodymyr Zelensky was born in 1978 in Kryvyi Rih, an industrial city in central Ukraine.
He studied law, then chose comedy, founding the troupe Kvartal 95.
The troupe grew into a production company with hit television shows.
In the sitcom Servant of the People, he played a teacher who becomes president.
He announced his candidacy on December 31, 2018.
In April 2019, he won the runoff with more than 73 percent, according to Al Jazeera.
He was sworn in on May 20, 2019, a political novice.
Nearly five years into the full-scale war, he leads a country at war with Russia.
But before the bridges were hit, there was a warning.

visivo.testo: But before the bridges were hit, there was a warning.

scene.testo: On Monday, Zelensky said there was information that the Russians had prepared a strike, according to AFP.
He told Ukrainians: "Tonight, overnight, and throughout tomorrow, please pay attention to missile danger alerts."

citazione.testo: Tonight, overnight and throughout tomorrow, please pay attention to missile danger alerts

scene.testo: He also warned Moscow, in his words:

citazione.testo: for every one of their evils there will be our just response

scene.testo: That day, Zelensky said Ukraine joined online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European officials.
Zelensky said it was the first time European representatives had taken part in talks with US and Ukrainian negotiators on finding a way forward with Russia.
Zelensky said the European delegation included France, Britain, Germany, Poland, Italy and EU negotiators; Kushner also listed NATO among the participants.
Kushner said Washington was committed to strong, credible security guarantees and a path toward EU membership.
Air raid alerts were declared in Kyiv at 11:36 p.m., and Klitschko later reported preliminary hits on the bridges.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko said that, according to preliminary information, the Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro were hit.
He said the strikes damaged critical infrastructure systems, with some areas experiencing disruptions to water and heating supplies.

citazione.testo: Some areas are experiencing disruptions to water and heating supplies

scene.testo: Eight major bridges cross the Dnipro. About three million residents rely on them.
The extent of damage to Kyiv's bridges remained unclear, Kyiv Post reported.
Several of Kyiv's bridges were also targeted by Russian drones in October.
The Northern Bridge was hit on November 7, closing it fully, according to NV via Archynewsy.
The Institute for the Study of War warned this may be an effort to split Kyiv's power network along the river.
Elsewhere, three people were injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkasy region.
Moscow has not, in these reports, explained its aims for the Kyiv strikes.
Zelensky said Russia is receiving dozens of ballistic missiles from North Korea every month.
He asked allies to help in 'countering Russian global banditry'.
He also said Europe has missiles that can deliver truly effective strikes.
Putin made a rare acknowledgment on October 1 that Ukrainian strikes had cost Russia about 1% of its GDP, according to AP.
Diplomacy is stuck. Last week's US-led talks ended without a breakthrough, but with a major prisoner exchange agreed.
After talks in Abu Dhabi, Putin reiterated hardline territorial demands, AFP reports.
He said any deployment of foreign troops would be seen in Moscow as a 'continuation of war'.
Zelensky ruled out handing over territory, and Kyiv refuses to cede Donbas areas it still holds.
A summit in Shenzhen between Xi, Trump and Putin is set for November 19, and US officials say Trump is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine.
Kushner said preparations had begun for the agenda of the next multilateral meeting, which the sides are working to convene in the near future.
On the Kerch Bridge, the question is simple: how long will repairs last, and what comes next?
Russia says the damage is minor. Ukraine has not detailed its operation. Independent verification is limited.
Two bridges in Kyiv. One bridge in Crimea. And a war that keeps moving.

visivo.testo: A WAR OF BRIDGES, STILL MOVING
